title: Derivatization and Determination of Structural Monosaccharides in Fungal Exopolysaccharide
author: Tayebeh Fooladi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.5j8g4rw
materials: 9- Keep the creamy powder of EPS at 4 °C for further analyses. Note: This procedure can repeat four times to purify the polysaccharide. EPS derivatization protocol Preparation of the stock solutions 1. Prepare 0.1 M Hydrochloric acid (HCl) stock solution: add 0.81 ml HCl (37%) to 25 ml D.W. firstly and bring to a final volume of 100 ml with D.W. 2. Prepare Ethanoic acid solution by mixing 4.3 ml of 0.1 M HCl stock solution with 4ml D.W. and bring to a final volume of 100 ml with absolute Methanol. 3. Make a solution of 15 ml Pyridine (anhydrous, 99.8 %, Sigma-Aldrich) in 30 ml D.W. 4. Prepare 2 M Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) to a final volume of 100 ml in a volumetric flask using D.W. Note: Pyridine is a toxic liquid and be careful when working with. Note: Pyridine should be prepared as a daily solution and kept at -20 ºC freezer 30 min before starting the experiments, but avoid freezing completely. 5. Prepare 1 N sulfuric acid using H2SO4 (98%) to a final volume of 100 ml using D.W. 6. Prepare 0.1 N sulfuric acid solution to a final volume of 100 ml using D.W. 7. Make a solution of sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) (5%; w/v) using D.W. Monosaccharides standard preparation 1. Prepare the pure monosaccharides (Sigma Aldrich), and dilute in D.W. with concentration of 0.01 M. Note: Monosaccharides include d (Glucose, Galactose and Mannose) [3-5], the standard procedure is followed according to the alditol derivatization protocol as below, except the hydrolyzation step.

steps.title: Hydrolyze Crude Exopolysaccharide (EPS)
steps.instruction: Hydrolyze the crude EPS using trifluoroacetic acid (TFA) under reflux.

substeps.instruction: Add 15 mg of crude extracted EPS and 10 ml 2 M TFA to a glass bottle and stir well with a magnetic stirrer.
Transfer the solution to a 50 ml round-bottom flask and assemble a reflux apparatus.
Perform hydrolysation at 121 ºC for 3 hr.
Evaporate excess acid at 50 ºC using a vacuum pump until a viscous carbohydrate syrup is obtained.
Dissolve the syrup in 5 ml distilled water (D.W.), stir until completely dissolved, and store at 4 ºC.

steps.title: Reduce Carbohydrates to Alditols
steps.instruction: Reduce the carbonyl groups of the carbohydrates using sodium borohydride.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the carbohydrate solution to a 250 ml round-bottom flask with a magnet and clamp to a magnetic stirrer.
Slowly add 40 mg Sodium borohydride (NaBH4) and stir for 1 hr at room temperature (RT).
Add a few drops of acetic acid to stop the reaction.
Continue stirring for an additional 20 min.
Evaporate the excess acid to obtain a syrup.

steps.title: Acetylate Alditols
steps.instruction: Perform acetylation of the reduced sugars to create alditol acetates.

substeps.instruction: Under a fume hood, add 3 ml ethanoic acid solution to the syrup, let sit for 1 min, and evaporate the acid; repeat this process 3 times.
Add 5 ml acetic anhydride (AC2O) and 0.12 ml concentrated H2SO4 to the syrup.
Place the mixture in a hot water bath at 80 ºC for 1 hr, then allow to cool at RT.
Add a previously prepared highly cold (-20 ºC) aqueous solution of pyridine and agitate on a magnetic stirrer for 20 min.

steps.title: Extract and Purify Derivatized Saccharides
steps.instruction: Isolate the alditol acetates using chloroform extraction and washing steps.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the solution to a 250 ml decanter funnel clamped under a fume hood.
Add an equal volume of chloroform, close the cap, and invert the funnel 3 times.
Collect the bottom chloroform phase (containing derivatized saccharides) and discard the upper aqueous/pyridine phase.
Rinse the funnel with an equal volume of D.W., invert 3 times, and collect the chloroform phase.
Wash the chloroform phase sequentially with 10 ml 1 N H2SO4, 10 ml 5% (w/v) sodium bicarbonate, and D.W.
Dry the solution over 10 mg sodium sulfate (Na2SO4), filtrate to remove salt, and evaporate under vacuum to obtain a syrup.
Dissolve the syrup in a few drops of chloroform.
Transfer immediately to a freezer and store at -20 ºC.

steps.title: Analyze via GC-MS
steps.instruction: Analyze the alditol acetates using a Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry system.

substeps.instruction: Use an HP-6890 coupled to an HP-5973 mass selective detector with a 30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 μm HP-5 MS capillary column.
Inject 1 µl of sample using an auto sampler injector.
Set the oven temperature program: 50 °C (hold 1 min) → 5 °C/min to 100 °C (hold 3 min) → 10 °C/min to 240 °C (hold 10 min) → 250 °C (hold 15 min).
Regulate auxiliary line and source temperatures at 285 °C.
Operate MS in electron impact (70 eV) using argon as collision gas at 1 mTorr.
Perform separation from 250 °C to 285 °C at a rate of 1 °C/min.

description:
Method details: Isolation and cultivation of the microorganism 1. Preserve the collected biological sample (here, fruiting body of the fungus) at 4 °C in refrigerator. 2. Isolate fungus on PDA, incubate the petri plates at 28 °C for 7 days [1]. Note: Store mycelial culture of the isolate on Agar slants in test tubes in 4 °C and sub-
culture monthly. 3. Set up the fermentation experiments in 250 ml Erlenmeyer flasks containing 50 ml semi-
synthetic culture medium. Note: The culture medium containing (g/l); glucose (30.0); yeast extract (6.0); polypeptone (2.0); MgSO4.7H2O (0.5); K2HPO4 (0.5) and MnSO4.5H2O (0.5) [2]. 4. Punch out a piece of approximately 25 mm2 of the agar medium with a sterile scalpel, homogenize by potter-type homogenizer and transfer it into the steam sterilized pre-culture medium containing (LB) broth. 5. Incubate at 30 ºC on a rotary shaking incubator at 150 rpm for 2 days. 6. Transfer an aliquot of 10 ml from the pre-culture medium to inoculate 100 ml of semi-
synthetic culture medium in 500 ml Erlenmeyer flasks. 7. Incubate the cultures at 30 °C on a rotary shaker, 150 rpm up to 7 days. Crude exopolysaccharide extraction protocol 1. Collect a homogenous sample from shake flasks, centrifuge at 8000× g for 20 min. 2. Mix supernatant with four volumes of ethanol 96% (v/v) and keep overnight at 4 ºC. 3. Centrifuge at 10,000× g for 20 min. 4. Collect the precipitate which is estimated as crude EPS. 5. Evaporate the excess ethanol from polysaccharide precipitates; air-dry overnight. 6. Adjust the pH of the raw EPS, 0.1% (w/v) aqueous solution, pH 3 with 10% trichloroacetic acid solution, and stir at 4 °C for 2 hr and then centrifuge for 30 min at 30,000× g. 8. Precipitate the supernatant with 4 volumes of absolute ethanol from the aqueous phase and resolve again in D.W.
